info.title: Freeport Seller API
info.description:
One API for every lane and every kind of seller software.

Send your key as `Authorization: Bearer fp_live_…`. Money is a decimal string in the row's currency, ids are prefixed ULIDs, times are ISO 8601 UTC. Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`; a 429 carries `Retry-After`. Errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "requestId" } }`.

requestId.description: Quote this when asking for help.

details.description: Detail a client can act on, where there is any: field-level detail on a 400, and on a 409 that refuses something the order’s state no longer allows (`illegal_transition`, `order_being_accepted`, `order_not_open`, `nothing_to_dispute`, and `no_open_dispute` once the order has left `disputed`) an object `{ "state": "…" }` naming the state the order is in. Read the order again and act on that.

paused.description: True while the platform is offering nothing of yours to buyers.

SellingState.description: The platform’s own switch over everything you sell, beside `holiday_mode`, which is yours. `missed_orders`: paid orders ran out without an answer, and a person resumes from the seller dashboard, not before `resume_after`; a key cannot. `declines`: you declined a burst of paid orders (three inside 24 hours, unless the seller standards say otherwise), the account is flagged for our review, and a person resumes from the seller dashboard the same way. `sales_limit`: your account is new, and its orders over the last thirty days have come to what a new account may sell; it lifts by itself as those orders pass thirty days and as your account builds a record, or when we review it. `order_limit` was this limit on open orders before it became a category’s: it is now in `selling_by_lane`, and an account paused for it before then is returned within a minute. `account.selling_changed` carries the same facts when they change.

paused.description: True while the platform is offering nothing of yours in this category.

LaneSelling.description: The platform’s own switch over one category. `order_limit`: you are restricted in this category and have as many of its orders open as you may; it lifts by itself when one is delivered, and your other categories are not affected. `account.lane_selling_changed` carries the same facts, with the category, when they change. A pause of the whole account is `selling`, and is not repeated here.

rank_level.description: 1 to 6, lowest first. The rank this month’s sales hold, and what a sale costs.

currency.description: The currency your account is paid in: your listings are priced in it, and `month_sales` is in it.

month_sales.description: A decimal string in the row's currency. Never a float.

trading_status.description: `active`, or `suspended`: reads keep working, writes that start something are refused.

selling_by_lane.description: The platform’s own switch over each category, by category.

reliability.description: The worst that your record of answering and delivering paid orders holds you to in any category: see `reliability_by_lane`. The figures and the orders behind them are on the seller dashboard.

reliability_by_lane.description: What your record holds you to in each category, judged on that category’s orders alone. `restricted` in a category limits how many of its orders you may have open at once and refuses new listings there with `selling_restricted`, until its figures recover; a restriction in any category also stops your rank rising.

payout_hold_days.description: The days your track record asks a sale to wait before its proceeds can be withdrawn. A category can ask for longer: see `payout_holds`.

payout_holds.description: What a sale completing today waits in each category, in days: the longer of `payout_hold_days` and the category’s own. A category that is not open for selling is left out. An order already completed keeps the date it was given.

available.description: A decimal string in the row's currency. Never a float.

pending.description: A decimal string in the row's currency. Never a float.

payout_hold_days.description: The days your track record asks a sale to wait. What is pending is released order by order, each on the `payout.release_at` of its own order.

state.description: `requested`: waiting for a person to review it. `approved`: checked and cleared, being sent. `sent`: on its way, `provider_ref` holds the reference; final for a withdrawal paid by hand. `paid`: in your bank account. `returned`: your bank sent it back, and the money is back in your balance. `rejected`: declined, and the money is back in your balance. `failed`: it could not be sent, and the money is back in your balance.

speed.description: `batch` is a standard withdrawal, approved and sent every business day once its money is past the payout hold. `express` is sent sooner, and only sellers may ask for one.

amount.description: What was asked for, and what left your available balance when the request was made. A withdrawal to your bank account is paid in full and costs nothing; one paid by hand has its fee taken out of it. `net` is what you receive.

fee.description: What the withdrawal cost: nothing for one to your bank account, which the payout fee on your sales pays for; for one paid by hand, what the published fee schedule priced its speed at when it was asked for (the fees page lists the prices). 0.00 on a batch withdrawal asked for before 15 October 2026, when the batch was free.

net.description: What is paid to you: all of `amount` for a withdrawal to your bank account, `amount` less `fee` for one paid by hand.

destination_hint.description: Where it was sent, masked as the Payouts page masks it. The full address is never returned by the API.

rail.description: How it is paid: `bank`, to your bank account; `skrill`, by hand.

provider_ref.description: The payment provider’s reference, once it is sent. Null until then.

reason.description: The sentence shown beside the withdrawal on the Payouts page when it was rejected or failed. Null otherwise.

filed_for.description: Null where you asked for it. `unwithdrawn`: Freeport filed it for sales you had not withdrawn 75 days after they were paid. `closing`: Freeport filed it before your account was closed.

id.description: The ledger entry this line is.

type.description: The ledger posting this entry belongs to, by the kind the ledger records it under. Known kinds: `order.completed` (a sale credited, pending), `order.dispute_completed` (a sale a dispute ended for you), `order.dispute_split` (your share of a split dispute), `payout.hold_released` (a sale's hold ended: one line out of pending, one into available), `payout.requested` (a withdrawal asked for), `payout.rejected` and `payout.failed` (its money back), `payout.returned` (your bank sent it back, and the money is back in your balance), `refund.seller_fee` (the refund fee you carry when a sale is refunded after you accepted it, taken from your available balance), `payout.topped_up` (Freeport's own money added so a withdrawal it filed reaches the smallest payout your bank can be sent), `chargeback.sale_held` (a completed sale's money held while the buyer's bank disputes its payment, out of pending, available or both), `chargeback.sale_released` (that money back where it came from, once the bank decides for you or Freeport carries the loss), `chargeback.loss_freeport` (your part of an order the bank's chargeback ended, yours again as a sale's money, pending, when Freeport carries the loss), `chargeback.loss_undone` (a loss placed on you undone: what it took that never left your balance, available again), `chargeback.given_back` (the same: what it took that had left your balance, sent back and available), `chargeback.seller_fee` (the payment provider's fee you carry on an order a chargeback ended, taken from your available balance), `affiliate.commission_accrued` and `affiliate.hold_released` (a partner's commission, on lines from before 16 October 2026: since then commissions are a balance of their own and appear in none of these lines). A new kind is added here as the ledger gains one; a client should show one it does not know rather than fail.

amount.description: Gross amount: `net` plus `fee`. A sale before the commission and the payout fee; a withdrawal as sent, before any fee taken from it.

fee.description: The fee assessed in this posting, positive when charged. A sale's commission as the order kept it (a coupon already off), its payout fee, and any fees you owed that the sale paid; a withdrawal's fee taken from your balance, negative on the line that gives it back (a withdrawal to your bank account carries none). 0.00 where none was assessed, and on a dispute split, which stores none.

net.description: The impact on your balance: positive adds to it, negative takes from it. Summing `net` over every line is your available plus your pending balance, `GET /v1/me/balance`.

status.description: `pending` for money still inside the payout hold, `available` for money you can withdraw.

available_on.description: When the money becomes yours to withdraw: a pending sale's release date, and the line's own moment for money that is available. Null where no date was fixed.

source.description: What this line is for: the order or the withdrawal, or the refund's or the chargeback's own id on a line posted under it (`refund.seller_fee`, `chargeback.seller_fee`, `chargeback.loss_undone`, `chargeback.given_back`). Null for a partner's commission, whose order is somebody else's purchase.

payout_fee.description: The payout fee on the price, taken with your commission, which makes your withdrawals to your bank free. No coupon changes it. Zero on an order placed before the payout fee existed.

character_name.description: The character to deliver to in the game. Null where the order needs none: an account, a gift card, or a top up that is not handed over in the game.

player_id.description: The player ID to load, for a top up loaded by one. As the buyer typed it. Null on every other order.

zone_id.description: The zone or server number that goes with the player ID, for a top up whose delivery method is UID + Zone ID. Null on every other order.

delivery_methods.description: How the seller offered to hand the currency over, copied from the listing at checkout. The buyer picks one in the order chat. Null when the listing is not currency or its game has no method list.

release_at.description: When this order’s proceeds become withdrawable. Decided when the order completes and never brought forward afterwards. Null until then, and on an order that ended without a sale.

hold_days.description: The days that date was worked out from: the longer of what your track record and the order’s category asked for on the day it completed.

seller.description: The published schedule row your commission was priced by.

payout.description: The published schedule row your payout fee was priced by. Null where the standard rate priced it, as on every order placed before the payout fee existed.

seq.description: Strictly increasing, in one series across every order on the platform rather than per order, so gaps between one order's events are normal; the number a consumer orders by.

bands.description: A range or count whose unit price changes along it: the first unit of each stretch, ascending from min. A count of n pays its units as a range from 0 to n would, and its first stretch also covers the units below its start. Priced in `bands` (or `rate_bands` with `rate_by`).

rate_by.description: The key of a choice option whose chosen value sets this option's unit price. Priced in `rates` (or `rate_bands` with `bands`).

per.description: Rates for this option are quoted per this many units.

step.description: Values move in steps of this many units from min.

repeat.description: A count that repeats the whole job: the price of one is multiplied by it, and it has no rate of its own.

pricing.description: How a choice, or the extras by default, move the price: basis points (`choice_bps`, `flag_bps`) or money (`choice_prices`, `flag_prices`).

additionalProperties.description: A decimal string in the row's currency. Never a float.

per_unit.description: A rate per unit, keyed by a range or number option with no `bands` and no `rate_by`.

rates.description: The rate per unit by the value chosen on the option named in `rate_by`, keyed by the option then that value. A value missing here is not for sale.

rate_bands.description: Both at once, for a banded range or count with `rate_by`: keyed by the option, then the chosen value, then the stretch's first unit.

choice_bps.description: Basis points per chosen value, keyed by a percent choice option then its value.

choice_prices.description: Money added per chosen value, keyed by a flat choice option then its value. A value missing here is not for sale.

flag_bps.description: Basis points per percent extra offered. An extra missing here is not for sale.

flag_prices.description: Money per flat extra offered. An extra missing here is not for sale.

ladder.description: The price of each division of a ladder option, keyed by the option then by the rank the step climbs out of (gold_ii is Gold II to Gold I). A climb costs the sum of its divisions. A division missing here is not for sale.

not_offered.description: Values of a choice option this booster does not take, keyed by the option.

post.description:
The synthetic buyer places and pays for an order on one of your listings through the real checkout, so `order.paid` reaches your endpoint by the production path. Then accept and deliver it as you would any order, and drive the buyer from the routes below. Sandbox only.

Scope `orders:write`. Spends the `writes` budget (120 a minute for a new seller).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Any string you choose, up to 200 characters. A repeat within a day gets the first response back with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and the write never runs twice. A first response too large to keep is replayed under its original status with `Idempotent-Body: omitted` and the `ReplayedWithoutBody` schema in place of the body: the write completed, so read the resource for its current state. A repeat while the first is running is a 409 `idempotency_in_progress`. If the first attempt ended in a 5xx, or never reported its outcome, the repeat is a 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown`: the write may have landed before the failure, so check whether it did, then use a new key. A 4xx refusal wrote nothing and releases the key, so a corrected request runs. If the key cannot be checked the request is refused with 503 `idempotency_unavailable`: send it again with the same key.
